lines.text: There was a light on in Module 3.
And a shadow *moved.*
I pulled myself to the window.
Inside, floating, was a woman.
She was writing in a notebook. Numbers. Like mine.
Her hair floated around her head. She looked thin. Tired.
Then she looked up.
And saw a spacesuit at her window.
We both froze.
Two people, three feet apart, on a station where each of us was supposed to be alone.
She put her hand on the glass.
She wrote something on a page, and held it up.
Who are you?
I couldn't write in a spacesuit. So I pointed at the name on my chest.
Cole.
She read it. Her lips moved. Cole.
Then the sun set, and her window went black.
Back inside, I couldn't stop shaking.
She was real. She had been real for one hundred fifty-one days.
Every knock. Every S.O.S. That was her.
Day one hundred fifty-two. Three in the morning.
Three knocks.
This time, I knocked back. Three.
My hand was shaking.
Silence.
For a long time, nothing.
Then Morse. Slow. One letter at a time.
I wrote each letter down.
They.
Told.
Me.
They told me you were *dead.*
